references.text: The preceding verses describe the conflict over the wells Esek and Sitnah. The context of strife makes it meaningful that Isaac called the third well Rehoboth ('room'), because the Lord had finally made room for them.
Isaac sows in the land and harvests a hundredfold, and the Lord blesses him so that he becomes rich. This shows God's blessing, which culminates in the Lord making room for them in verse 22.
God promises to make Abraham very fruitful (hifritikha). Isaac's statement 'we shall be fruitful in the land' (ufarinu ba'arets) in 26:22 is a fulfillment of this promise.
The psalmist says that God gave him room in distress (batsár hirkhávta lí). This uses the same root word (rakhav) as Rehoboth, and expresses the same theme: God gives room when it is tight.

Isaiah urges to enlarge the place of your tent and stretch out your curtains, for descendants will inherit the nations. The theme of God's expansion parallels Isaac's experience of the Lord making room in 26:22.

Psalm 107 describes how God turns the desert into springs of water and lets people settle down, sow, and plant, and He blesses them so that they multiply. This reflects the theme of fruitfulness and expansion in Gen 26:22.
Both verses illustrate how God's gift of 'room' (ro/place) is a prerequisite for fruitfulness and blessing after conflict.
Both verses show a parallel where a patriarch names something as a testimony that God has made them fruitful in a foreign or conflicted land.
